Sencha & steamed green tea.d: Cold-hardy, thick-leaved green tea of Saitama and north-west Tokyo, finished by the Sayama-bi-ire roast devised in 1802.
Sencha & steamed green tea.dt: region: Musashino Plateau · finish: Sayama-bi-ire (steamed, roasted on washi)

Sencha & steamed green tea.d: The classic Japanese tea cultivar, 67.6% of tea-field area in 2021 (about 75% in 2010).
Early-budding cultivar for southern Japan, mostly sold as fukamushi sencha; second in Kagoshima.
High-yield, cold-resistant cultivar high in catechins, bitter if over-infused.

Gyokuro & kabusecha.d: Cultivar with high amino acids, suited to shaded teas such as gyokuro.
Late-budding cultivar used in matcha and gyokuro, often blended with Yabukita.
Sixth-ranked cultivar at 0.7% of area; not to be confused with Saemidori.

brands.d: Uji tea house founded in 1832, known for matcha sweets and its main-store tea room.
